summary: Elevated 5xx rate after customer enabled model-pinning; prefetch/KV-cache thrash causing upstream runtime restarts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (CartographAI, dedicated) began seeing sustained elevated 5xx responses from Redwood API beginning 2026-03-10 08:15 UTC after they enabled model-pinning to redwood-gptx-13b-quant-v2 for high-consistency routing. Errors observed across streaming and non-streaming endpoints.

Impact:
- ~18% error-rate elevated 5xx for the customer's tenant over a 45-minute window (api-gateway 502/503/504).
- Streaming sessions experienced frequent disconnects; customers reported partial responses and retries.
- Latency for successful requests increased 3x during peak.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool for CartographAI in prod-us-east; autoscaler configured with burst headroom of 2 nodes.
- Model pinned to redwood-gptx-13b-quant-v2; pinning took effect at 2026-03-10T08:12:30Z.

Steps to reproduce (from customer repro script):
1) Pin model on tenant config to redwood-gptx-13b-quant-v2 and route 90% of traffic to streaming endpoint.
2) Run steady small-batch (1-2 tokens per step) streaming traffic at ~150 rps for 20 minutes.
3) Observe increasing 5xx rate; runtime pod restarts visible in tenant pool.

Observed logs (examples):
- apigw: "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers\n (errno=104)" correlating with 502 spikes.
- runtime stderr: repeated lines of "kv_cache_eviction: thrashing detected, evicting prefixes" followed by "kernel_fallback: switching to slower execution path" and then "fatal: runtime OOM, killed by oom-killer".
- node exporter: GPU memory fragmentation high, sudden jumps in host OOM events.

Preliminary findings:
- Timeline shows pinning caused hot-spotting onto a subset of GPU nodes that had older kernel patches and a smaller prefetch queue configuration.
- Small, high-concurrency streaming requests cause frequent KV cache churn; cache evictions cascade into increased prefetch activity and repeated kernel fallback on a fraction of runtime pods.
- Kernel fallback path is significantly slower and increases per-request memory pressure; combined with aggressive prefetch, some runtimes hit OOM and restart. Restarts cause downstream upstream disconnects -> apigw 502/503/504 and elevated customer error rates.

Temporary mitigations applied (by infra on 2026-03-10):
- Rolled back the tenant-specific model pin to allow smart routing (completed 08:35 UTC) — immediate error-rate improvement to ~2% within 6 minutes.
- Increased prefetch queue window from 8 -> 16 for the affected runtime nodes to reduce churn (08:42 UTC) as a hotfix.
- Temporarily increased dedicated pool headroom by +2 GPU nodes (08:50 UTC) to reduce hot-spotting pressure.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering: build a runtime patch to limit prefetch concurrency per-tenant when KV cache thrash detected (priority).
- Apply kernel patch to affected node image and roll once canary validated (linked PR).
- Product/Support: add a tenant-level soft-circuit-breaker for high error/oom signals to divert traffic to fallback model variant automatically.
- Ops: add an automated alarm for "prefetch_thrash_rate" and a dashboard panel correlating kv_evictions -> kernel_fallback -> OOM restarts.

Links and artifacts:
- Customer support logs: s3://redwood-support/cartographai/2026-03-10/prefetch-thrash.tar.gz
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant-prefetch/CartographAI-prefetch-overview
- Slack thread: #support-cartographai (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/CS-1234)
- Related PR (runtime throttling prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821

investigation_notes:
Root cause hypothesis: tenant model-pinning concentrated traffic onto nodes with older kernel/fallback characteristics; small-batch streaming pattern created high prefix churn in the KV cache triggering prefetch amplification and kernel fallback which increased memory pressure -> OOMs -> pod restarts -> apigw 5xx amplification. Confirmed by correlated timestamps across apigw traces, runtime eviction logs, and node oom events.

Evidence:
- Exact match between pin activation (08:12:30Z) and initial rise in kv_eviction metrics.
- Runtime process core dumps show allocation spike pattern consistent with repeated fallback execution path.
- Reverting pin returned traffic to balanced routing and reduced thrash immediately.
resolution: Mitigation applied: rolled back customer model pin and increased prefetch queue; long-term fix planned (runtime prefetch throttling + kernel image roll). Postmortem and ETA to be published after Eng validation.
